title: First African-American woman doctor of medicine
summary: Rebecca Lee Crumpler qualified in medicine in 1864, cared for freed people after the Civil War, and published A Book of Medical Discourses in 1883.
why: Opened medicine to Black women in the United States.

unsung.contribution: Became the first African-American woman doctor of medicine and wrote an early medical book for women and children.
unsung.recognition: Ignored by male physicians in her lifetime, she lay in an unmarked grave for 125 years until 2020.
